trigger: a server restart drops all in-memory confirmed state; the first tick repopulates unconfirmed_cache_ fleet-wide and each such agent's next heartbeat drives a full reconcile_one inline, gated only by the per-agent 60s claim, not by kMaxDispatchesPerTick
summary: Post-restart reconnect burst is paced by the per-tick cap on the periodic path but not on the heartbeat fast path - increases heartbeat-processing load fleet-wide during a mass-reconnect window without corrupting state.
waiver_rationale: Bounded blast radius (individually rate-limited, idempotent); quarantine population characterized as manually-curated security events, not high-volume. Queued alongside the related performance finding on the gateway batch path.

trigger: the conjunction of Postgres pool degradation and one or more quarantined-unconfirmed agents present in one gateway-routed BatchHeartbeat RPC, which loops sequentially and invokes the reconcile hook inline per entry with no per-entry latency isolation from the batch
summary: A slow-but-not-throwing pool acquire on one quarantined agent in a batch stalls the whole sequential loop, delaying the ACK for every other (potentially thousands of) agents riding the same batch. The one finding from this review worth prioritizing.
waiver_rationale: Non-blocking per derivation (MEDIUM, not HIGH/CRITICAL) but flagged as the highest-priority follow-up of this Gate 3 round. Suggested remediations: skip the hook on the gateway batch path (rely on tick()'s 20s backstop), give the reconcile attempt a fast non-blocking pool probe, or move the dispatch off the RPC handler thread. Re-scope against the Gate 3 fix round's HeartbeatIngestion locking change before filing.

trigger: a Heartbeat-RPC handler thread is inside quarantine_reconcile_fn_(...) (blocking Postgres + gRPC-dispatch I/O) when server.cpp's stop() sequence nulls the unsynchronized std::function and then .reset()s the QuarantineContainmentReconciler its closure captures, past only a bounded (not quiescence-guaranteeing) gRPC drain deadline
policy_floor: ownership/lifetime defect (cpp-safety blocking contract) - unsynchronized cross-thread callback reassignment racing operator(), plus a post-reset dangling capture
summary: quarantine_reconcile_fn_ was a bare std::function with no synchronization against concurrent teardown - a genuine cross-thread use-after-free window during a routine rolling restart against live heartbeat traffic, not merely theoretical.
waiver_rationale: Fixed by adding std::shared_mutex quarantine_reconcile_mu_: ingest() holds a shared_lock for the FULL duration of the callback (not just to copy it, which would not restore the drain-barrier property), set_quarantine_reconcile_fn takes a unique_lock, making set(nullptr) an actual drain barrier before .reset() runs. Verified via a deterministic latch-based regression test (test_heartbeat_ingestion.cpp), mutation-tested by temporarily removing the lock and confirming the test fails, then restoring. Scoped to quarantine_reconcile_fn_ only, per operator convention against sweeping fixes onto unauthored pre-existing sibling code (guardian_reconcile_fn_ has the same shape, recorded as a separate follow-up candidate in the resource ledger, not fixed here).

policy_floor: Resource Ledger omission on a C++ diff

waiver_rationale: Cured in this round: governance.d/3425-quarantine-reconnect.u21SjI.resource-ledger.md written (enumerating the new thread, the new shared_mutex, the 5 borrowed Deps pointers, the dispatch_fn/now_fn captures, the reused PG-lease pattern, and the test-only thread/latch usage), plus this run ledger backfilled with Gate 2 and Gate 3 findings.

trigger: mark_endpoint_applied fails with a non-"device is not quarantined" (generic store) error while agents_reached>0
summary: Unlike the symmetric confirm-failure branch, the apply-failure branch on a generic store error did not extend backoff, so a sustained QuarantineStore write outage re-dispatched a fresh quarantine-apply command every fixed ~60s instead of backing off exponentially like every other repeated-failure path.
waiver_rationale: Fixed by mirroring the confirm branch's next_backoff/next_eligible_at escalation on the generic-error path.

trigger: docs/user-manual/audit-log.md's quarantine.reapply row states 'There is no result=denied/failure shape today' — false since the Gate 2 audit_unstamped fix (commit 8e28fd80d)
policy_floor: an I7 doc-staleness finding that conceals security-relevant behavior
summary: A doc claim about the containment audit trail's shape contradicted shipped, tested code — a query or runbook built on 'failure is impossible here' silently misses a real signal (a store-degradation event during containment re-application).
waiver_rationale: Fixed: added the third result=failure shape to the row. Same-sink sweep performed (not a separate finding): docs/prometheus/yuzu-alerts.yml's alert annotation and docs/observability-conventions.md's #3425 paragraph were checked and judged accurate as-is — neither claims shape-exclusivity — so deliberately left untouched, a decision recorded here for Gate 8's docs-writer rather than a miss.

trigger: the offline-skip branch in reconcile_one consumed the full per-agent claim window (set at claim time, before the reachability check) regardless of how many times the device was found offline, so a stale claim could hold the FIRST post-reconnect heartbeat rate_limited
summary: security-hardening.md's 'fires within one heartbeat interval of reconnect' overclaimed speed for the feature's own headline scenario; real worst-case was up to a full claim window (60s prod) of residual wait plus a multi-leg confirm cycle (~2-3 min total).
classification: truth (doc overclaims measured behavior) + real behavior fix
waiver_rationale: Fixed in both code (offline skip now releases its claim immediately under lock, mirroring the K11/CDX-P1-05 no-spin reasoning already applied to the per-tick dispatch cap — safe because offline agents don't heartbeat, so nothing re-drives faster than the ~20s tick) and docs (the doc now describes the fast path accurately and states the full cycle spans a few heartbeat intervals, not one). New regression test proves the fix (immediate post-reconnect heartbeat dispatches despite a 60s claim override); mutation-test not run for this one-line change, proportionate given the code path is simple and directly analogous to an already-verified sibling fix (K11/CDX-P1-05).

trigger: an operator releases an actively-tracked quarantine record and immediately re-quarantines the same agent_id (different reason/whitelist) at any point during the reconciler's apply-poll-status-confirm cycle for the OLD record
summary: mark_endpoint_applied/mark_endpoint_confirmed's guarded UPDATE scoped only by agent_id+status='active', with no record-identity check — empirically reproduced: the confirmation stamp silently landed on a NEW unrelated record whose whitelist was never actually dispatched to the agent.
waiver_rationale: Fixed by adding QuarantineRecord::id (not exposed on REST/MCP) and threading it through the reconciler's state machine (AgentState::pending_record_id) into a third predicate on the guarded UPDATE (WHERE agent_id=$2 AND id=$3 AND status='active'). Also closes the narrower residual window between a completed apply and its follow-up verify read via an id-drift detection bail in the verify_first branch. Regression tests at both the store level (id-mismatch, mutation-tested by removing the id predicate and confirming the test fails) and the reconciler level (end-to-end race-and-recovery, proving the new record gets its own fresh apply). Not a routed-concerns clause-1 violation (the dispatch itself always used the stored whitelist correctly) — the defect was in which record the confirmation STAMP landed on afterward, not in what was dispatched.

trigger: the target agent's own quarantine.status reply is fully trusted as proof of endpoint containment, with no independent (network-side) corroboration — a compromised/tampered quarantine plugin on the specific already-suspect endpoint could reply state|active regardless of true firewall state
summary: Reporting agent (unhappy-path) derived CRITICAL per its own brief's stated E2 rule but explicitly flagged for orchestrator adjudication rather than asserting it outright, noting the trust decision is inherited from pre-existing #3127 semantics, not newly invented. Decomposed rather than adjudicated down (see gate4-finding-b1-truth-in-labeling and gate4-finding-b2-no-independent-verification) — no row here lowers this finding's own band; the gate obligation was discharged by fixing the newly-introduced half (B1).
waiver_rationale: Decomposition, not a weakening supersession: this row's band is left exactly as the reporting agent derived it (CRITICAL). E2-vs-E3 exposure classification is itself ambiguous (does a target agent replying about its OWN state, even falsely, constitute 'beyond its starting privilege'? argued but not settled) — recorded here rather than resolved unilaterally. Gate 8's security-guardian re-run is the independent check on this decomposition: if it disagrees the CRITICAL question reopens there, not silently closed by this round.

trigger: this PR newly introduces a durable last_confirmed_at stamp, a CONFIRMED-tagged success audit row, full unattended automation (no operator approval step, 20s-cadence background loop over the whole fleet), and suppression of further re-verification once confirmed=true — all presenting agent self-report as durable, automated 'confirmed containment' fact, without stating that it is unverified self-report
summary: The introduced-by-this-PR half of Finding B: once every surface honestly states that 'confirmed' means the agent's own report (cert-bound, not independently corroborated) and that the #881 gate does not key off it, the caller CAN tell what the fact actually is and the I3 (wrong result presented as correct) dissolves at its derived band — fixed via truth-in-labeling, not via weakening the underlying finding.
waiver_rationale: Fixed by adding an explicit self-report/not-independently-corroborated caveat to all three surfaces (audit-log.md's CONFIRMED shape description, security-hardening.md's Confirmation bullet, metrics.md's confirmed label description), each noting the #881 gate does not key off last_confirmed_at so a false confirmation narrows to false operator assurance, not a fleet-authorization bypass. This row authored by the orchestrator (source=collaborator, not governance-agent) as the resolution of unhappy-path's flagged-for-adjudication Finding B — Gate 8's security-guardian re-run should independently confirm this framing is accurate and sufficient, not merely well-written.

trigger: n/a - a standing design property, not a specific triggerable defect: no network-side (flow/ARP/traffic) cross-check exists anywhere to independently corroborate an agent-reported containment state
summary: The pre-existing half of Finding B: this trust boundary is inherited from #3127's already-shipped MCP already_active semantics, not newly invented by #3425. With B1's truth-in-labeling fix landed, this is an honestly-disclosed limitation, not a concealed one.
waiver_rationale: Suggested follow-up (not this PR's scope): correlate a 'confirmed' quarantine record against the network-quality/flow surface for continuing non-whitelisted egress as an independent corroboration signal. Queued alongside the other deferred-to-issue findings for operator approval before filing.

trigger: response_store->query fails (sustained degradation) while a device has a pending apply/status command — the pending-poll branch returns before computing timed_out, so the response-wait clock never advances and backoff never escalates
summary: A sustained response_store outage produces indefinite fixed-cadence stalling for a pending command rather than eventually timing out and escalating backoff like every other repeated-failure path in this state machine — fail-safe direction (never falsely declares timeout on a transient blip) but inconsistent with sibling paths.
waiver_rationale: Non-blocking; requires sustained store degradation (E5), delays (never loses) reconciliation. Queued alongside the other deferred-to-issue findings for operator approval before filing.

trigger: set_quarantine_reconcile_fn(nullptr)'s blocking unique_lock cannot return while ingest() holds the shared lock through a synchronous reconcile_one call chaining up to three I/O legs (get_status, gRPC dispatch, mark_endpoint_applied/confirmed) — worst case can exceed a typical 30s orchestrator termination grace period even though each leg is individually timeout-bounded
summary: The Gate 3 shared_mutex fix (closing a genuine UAF) trades it for a bounded-but-uncapped-by-any-watchdog shutdown delay under degraded Postgres/gRPC — same problem class this repo already has a precedent fix for (hard_exit.hpp, the Spark/Guardian detached-I/O-worker case), not yet applied here.
waiver_rationale: Non-blocking (requires co-occurring degradation at the exact moment of shutdown). Fix idea (bound the drain with a timed wait + log-and-proceed, or extend hard_exit's precedent) interacts with the Gate 3 shared_mutex fix and must be designed against the final shape of that lock, not improvised mid-round. Queued alongside the other deferred-to-issue findings for operator approval before filing.
